Title: Who is learning, and what do they already know?
Detail_lesson: A first-week volunteer, a manager who has done this for years, someone who has never used a laptop. Name them and where they start.
CustomInstruction: A person and what they know today.
ClaudeNote: Pitch every lesson at the winning answer: start from what they already know and never explain it again.

Title: What should they be able to do afterwards that they cannot do today?
Detail_lesson: Not what they should know. What they can do, on their own, the next time it matters.
ClaudeNote: Make the winning answer the course goal. Every lesson and every check must move toward it.

Title: Where and when will they take this?
Detail_lesson: On a phone between shifts, at a desk for an hour, in a room together. It changes how long a lesson can be.
CustomInstruction: A place and a length of time.
ClaudeNote: Fit the lesson length, the layout and the device to the winning answer.

Title: What mistake does a beginner make most often?
Detail_lesson: The thing every new person gets wrong in their first week.
ClaudeNote: Build a lesson or a check around each of the top answers, and show the right way next to the mistake.

Title: What do they need on day one, and what can wait?
Detail_lesson: Most training teaches too much too soon. Split the must-know from the nice-to-know.
CustomInstruction: Say which it is: day one, or later.
ClaudeNote: Put the day-one items in the first lesson. List the rest as later lessons on the Later list.

Title: How will we know someone has learned it?
Detail_lesson: A question they can answer, a task they can do, a mistake they no longer make.
ClaudeNote: Turn the winning answer into the check at the end of each lesson.

Title: What would you teach with a story instead of a rule?
Detail_lesson: People remember the time something went wrong far better than a list of rules.
CustomInstruction: Tell the story in two sentences.
ClaudeNote: Say which lesson the winning story fits, and draft it in a few lines.

Title: How would an expert teach this in five minutes, standing next to you?
Detail_lesson: No slides, no manual. What would they show you, and what would they skip?
CustomInstruction: What they show, and what they skip.
ClaudeNote: Say what you would cut or move from the lessons to match the winning answer.

Title: What would make someone want to finish?
Detail_lesson: Progress they can see, a reason to come back, something to show for it.
CustomInstruction: One thing that would keep you going.
ClaudeNote: Say what small feature would do the winning answer and what it would cost.

Title: Where did you get stuck in the lesson on the screen?
Detail_lesson: Look at what is on the wall. Where would a beginner stop and ask someone?
ClaudeNote: Fix the top answer first. Say in one line what you changed.

Title: Which question in the check felt unfair or unclear?
Detail_lesson: A good check question has one right answer that someone who learned the lesson would pick.
CustomInstruction: Name the question and what was wrong.
ClaudeNote: Rewrite the winning question and its feedback, and show it before and after.

Title: What example would make this click for people like us?
Detail_lesson: Our own words, our own place, our own kind of day.
ClaudeNote: Add the winning example to the lesson it fits.

Title: What should the next lesson cover?
Detail_lesson: The one thing someone would ask about the day after finishing this.
ClaudeNote: Put the winning answers on the Later list as the next lessons.

Title: What would make a manager trust this training?
Detail_lesson: Proof someone finished it, a short report, a sign-off. What would they need to see?
CustomInstruction: One thing a manager would check.
ClaudeNote: Add the winning answers to the Later list, and say which is the smallest to build.
